title: Efficient and Site-Specific Incorporation of 3-Nitro-Tyrosine Into Recombinant Proteins
author: Sarah B. McGee

chemically competent cells
BL21(DE3) (ThermoFisher, catalog number: EC

This E. coli strain is optimized for over-expression of target proteins driven by the T7 transcriptional promoter, which is commonly used in pET expression vectors. It carries a genomic copy of the T7 RNA polymerase gene under control of the lacUV5 promoter; induction with IPTG triggers T7 polymerase expression, leading to efficient transcription of the target gene and high yields of recombinant protein. Because this strain retains release factor 1 (RF1, the protein that terminates translation at TAG stop codons), expression of proteins containing TAG-encoded noncanonical amino acids can result in both truncated and full-length proteins. To prevent co-purification of truncated protein with the desired full-length protein, the use of a C-terminal affinity tag is recommended.
Δ A Δ fabR (Addgene, catalog number:
This strain is a fast-growing BL21(DE

derivative that lacks RF1, the protein responsible for terminating translation at TAG codons, and carries a spontaneous mutation in the fabR gene [18]. To preserve cellular viability and reduce unintended readthrough in the absence of RF1, endogenous TAG stop codons in 95 genes were converted to TAA or TGA. Compared to standard BL21(DE3), this strain may be preferred for protein expression because RF1 deletion enhances TAG codon suppression by GCE machinery and minimizes production of truncated proteins caused by premature termination at TAG sites. However, this introduces another issue: near-cognate suppression. If the level of nitroTyr aminoacylated tRNA concentration is insufficient, native tRNAs in the cell (e.g., Gln-tRNA) can suppress TAG codons and result in the insertion of natural amino acids at the intended site of nitroTyr encoding. Thus, optimizing nitroTyr concentration, as well as choosing the right cell line and media combination, is crucial for faithful incorporation of nitroTyr in B95 cells. See below in “Choice of cell line, GCE machinery system and media” for more information. Plasmids
pAJE-30- Mj- nitroTyr (Addgene, catalog number:

Machinery plasmid that enables encoding of nitroTyr at TAG codons. It expresses the Methanocaldococcus jannaschii (Mj)- TyrRS-nitroTyr “A7” [13] RS from a constitutive lpp promoter, as well as its cognate TAG codon-suppressing tRNA from a constitutive lpp promoter. This plasmid has spectinomycin resistance and contains a low-copy synthetic origin of replication [19,20] that is compatible with all standard origins, including ColE1/pBR322/pMB1, CDF, and p15A.
pAJE-30- Ma- nitroTyr (Addgene, catalog number:

Machinery plasmid that enables encoding of nitroTyr at TAG codons. It expresses the Methanomethylophilus alvus (Ma)- TyrRS-nitroTyr [14] RS from a constitutive GlnS promoter, as well as its cognate TAG codon-suppressing tRNA from a constitutive lpp promoter. This plasmid has spectinomycin resistance and contains a low-copy synthetic origin of replication [19,20] that is compatible with all standard origins, including ColE1/pBR322/pMB1, CDF, and p15A.
pET28-sfGFP WT (Addgene, catalog number:

Expresses wild-type sfGFP control protein with C-terminal His6 tag, under a T7 transcriptional promoter, kanamycin resistance, and pBR322 origin of replication. sfGFP is expressed by the addition of IPTG or lactose.
pET28-sfGFP TAG150 (Addgene, catalog number:
Same as above, except the sfGFP gene contains a TAG amber stop codon at site N
The TAG codon is used to direct the translational encoding of nitroTyr.

pET28-(GOI) WT (you must clone) Expresses your wild-type protein of interest (POI). You can clone the gene for your POI into the pET28 backbone by digesting with the restriction enzymes NcoI and XhoI, thus removing the gene for sfGFP. Your gene of interest (GOI) can then be put in using standard cloning techniques (ligation, Gibson Assembly, or SLiCE [21]).

pET28-(GOI) TAG (you must clone) Expresses your POI with nitroTyr encoded at a TAG codon. You can clone the gene for your POI into the pET28 backbone by digesting with the restriction enzymes NcoI and XhoI, thus removing the gene for sfGFP. Your GOI can then be put in using standard cloning techniques (ligation, Gibson Assembly, or SLiCE [21]). The codon where you want to encode nitroTyr can be changed to a TAG codon using site-directed mutagenesis. Choice of cell line, GCE machinery system, and media Successful, efficient encoding and purification of nitroTyr into proteins is strongly dependent on three key experimental variables: cell line, growth media, and the choice of GCE machinery. Optimal expression and purification yield full-length nitrated protein, with >95% of protein molecules containing nitroTyr at the intended site. However, suboptimal conditions can lead to three common side products, as shown in Figure 1 : (i) reduction of nitroTyr to 3-amino-tyrosine (aminoTyr) after successful incorporation, driven by the reducing environment of the cell; (ii) truncated protein, resulting from premature translation termination at TAG codons due to RF1; and (iii) misincorporation of glutamine via near-cognate suppression when the TAG codon is misread by endogenous tRNAs. Each of these outcomes is highly context-dependent. The greatest variable is the reduction of nitroTyr to aminoTyr, since this is influenced by oxygen availability, media composition, the POI, and the site of encoding. AminoTyr cannot be encoded by the nitroTyr RS/tRNA pairs, but cellular reductases can convert some encoded nitroTyr protein sites to aminoTyr, provided encoding sites are accessible and expression conditions are limited in oxygen. To minimize reduction, cultures should be well-aerated using baffled flasks, antifoam agents, and high shaking speeds (250–300 rpm) during expression. Truncation at TAG codons is inherent to RF1-positive strains such as BL21(DE3), but the effects of this issue can often be mitigated by using C-terminal purification tags, which allow for selective purification of full-length product. When C-terminal tagging is compatible with the POI, BL21(DE
is a practical and effective option. By contrast, B95(DE
Δ A Δ fabR is an RF1-deficient strain that enables truncation-free expression, supporting both N- and C-terminal tags without co-purification of prematurely truncated protein. However, the B95(DE

Δ A Δ fabR strain is more sensitive to expression inefficiencies: when intracellular nitroTyr is insufficient, near-cognate suppression may occur, most often resulting in glutamine incorporation at the intended nitroTyr site. In our experience, the likelihood of near-cognate suppression in B95(DE

Δ A Δ fabR is strongly influenced by media composition because nitroTyr uptake is significantly more efficient in “defined” media compared to “complex” media (e.g., ZY) containing tryptone and yeast extract. Poor uptake of nitroTyr in “complex” media leads to low efficiency of nitroTyr tRNA aminoacylation, allowing endogenous tRNA suppression of the UAG codon to occur readily in B95(DE
cells. In contrast, with BL21(DE

cells, RF1 will dominate over near-cognate suppression, leading to translational termination instead of mis-encoding of canonical aminos at the UAG codon. With sfGFP proteins, we observe up to 40% misincorporation when nitroTyr-containing proteins are expressed in B95(DE

Δ A Δ fabR cells using ZY “complex” media with either the Mj or Ma machinery systems. Switching to defined media effectively eliminates this issue and yields homogeneously nitrated, full-length protein in the B95(DE

Δ A Δ fabR strain. We have also observed that the M. alvus GCE system, while efficient, can be moderately toxic in B95 cells, likely due to background expression or metabolic burden. The M. jannaschii system is well tolerated in both BL21(DE

Δ A Δ fabR strains. From a practical standpoint, ZY media is easy to prepare and suitable for routine use, whereas defined media requires more components and preparation time. Given these considerations, we recommend the following strategies: • When truncation is acceptable and C-terminal tags are compatible with your POI, we recommend the M. alvus GCE system in BL21(DE

grown in ZY auto-induction media. This setup is robust, user-friendly, and produces high yields of homogeneously nitrated protein. The Ma nitroTyr GCE system can also be used to incorporate 3-chloroTyr, 3-bromoTyr, and 3-iodoTyr [13]. • When N-terminal purification tags are required, multi-site incorporation is desired, or truncation would compromise protein function, we recommend the M. jannaschii GCE system in B95(DE
Δ A Δ fabR , grown in defined auto-induction media, to ensure full-length, site-specifically nitrated protein without misincorporation. Table 1 summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of BL21(DE
Δ A Δ fabR expression hosts and media combination to help users select the most appropriate strategy for their specific expression system. Table

steps.title: Prepare LB/agar plates
steps.instruction: Mix 5 g tryptone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, and 7.5 g agar in 500 mL water, autoclave, cool, add antibiotics according to strain, pour 15–25 mL per plate and solidify.

substeps.instruction: Tryptone 1 % (w/v), Yeast extract 0.5 % (w/v), NaCl 1 % (w/v), Agar 1.5 % (w/v) to 500 mL.
Autoclave on liquid setting; swirl after cooling to mix molten agar.
For BL21(DE3): add 50 µL spectinomycin stock (100 µg/mL final) and 50 µL kanamycin stock (50 µg/mL final).
For B95(DE3) ΔAΔfabR: add 25 µL spectinomycin stock (50 µg/mL final) and 25 µL kanamycin stock (25 µg/mL final).
Pour 15–25 mL onto each sterile 100 mm plate, let solidify (~20 min).

steps.title: Prepare 2× YT medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 16 g tryptone, 10 g yeast extract, and 5 g NaCl in 1 L water, autoclave, cool to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Prepare SOC medium
steps.instruction: Combine 49 mL 2× YT, 0.5 mL 1 M MgSO₄·7H₂O (final 10 mM), 0.5 mL 40 % (w/v) α‑D‑glucose (final 0.4 % w/v ≈20 mM) to 50 mL total; sterilize components separately, mix under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Make 1 M MgSO₄·7H₂O by dissolving 12.3 g MgSO₄·7H₂O in water to 50 mL.
Make 40 % (w/v) α‑D‑glucose by dissolving 20 g glucose in water to 50 mL.
Autoclave MgSO₄ solution, glucose solution, and 2× YT separately; cool, then combine as above.

steps.title: Make kanamycin stock (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 g kanamycin in water to 10 mL (50 mg/mL), filter‑sterilize (0.2 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Make spectinomycin stock (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g spectinomycin sulfate in water to 10 mL (100 mg/mL), filter‑sterilize (0.2 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 25× M salts
steps.instruction: Dissolve 88.7 g Na₂HPO₄, 85.1 g KH₂PO₄, 66.9 g NH₄Cl, 17.8 g Na₂SO₄ in water to 1 L (final concentrations 0.625 M Na₂HPO₄, 0.625 M KH₂PO₄, 1.25 M NH₄Cl, 0.125 M Na₂SO₄).

substeps.instruction: Add salts to 900 mL water, stir until dissolved, then bring to 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare trace metal stock (5 000×)
steps.instruction: Make individual 30 mL 1× metal solutions (CaCl₂·2H₂O 20 mM, MnCl₂·4H₂O 10 mM, ZnSO₄·7H₂O 2 mM, CoCl₂·6H₂O 2 mM, CuCl₂ 2 mM, NiCl₂ 2 mM, Na₂SeO₃ 2 mM, Na₂MoO₄·2H₂O 2 mM, H₃BO₃ 2 mM, FeCl₃ 50 mM), sterilize (autoclave except FeCl₃, which is dissolved in 0.1 M HCl and filtered), then combine 500 µL of each (except FeCl₃) with 25 mL FeCl₃ solution to 50 mL total.

substeps.instruction: Prepare each metal stock using the masses listed.
Autoclave all except FeCl₃; dissolve FeCl₃ in 0.1 M HCl, filter.
Combine 500 µL of each 1× stock with 25 mL FeCl₃ stock; total volume 50 mL.

steps.title: Make 50× 5052 solution (500 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 12.5 g α‑D‑glucose (2.5 % w/v), 50 g α‑lactose (10 % w/v), and 125 mL glycerol (25 % v/v) in ~300 mL warm water, then bring to 500 mL, autoclave.

substeps.instruction: Heat gently; remove stir bar before microwaving.
Add remaining water after dissolution.

steps.title: Prepare nitro‑tyrosine stock (100 mM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 226 mg 3‑nitro‑L‑tyrosine in 225 µL 8 M NaOH, bring to 10 mL with water, vortex, aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C; prepare fresh before use.

steps.title: Prepare ZY medium (1 L)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract in 900 mL water, mix, bring to 1 L, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare ZY NIM and AIM (50 mL each)
steps.instruction: For each 50 mL tube add ZY medium (47 mL), 0.1 mL 1 M MgSO₄, 2 mL 25× M salts, 1 mL 50× 5052, 0.625 mL 40 % glucose (only NIM), 10 µL trace metal stock; adjust antibiotics: BL21 – 100 µg/mL spectinomycin, 50 µg/mL kanamycin; B95 – 50 µg/mL spectinomycin, 25 µg/mL kanamycin; prepare immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Do not pre‑mix concentrated stocks; add each directly to ZY medium.
For NIM include glucose; for AIM omit glucose.

steps.title: Prepare aspartate solution (5 % w/v, pH 7.5)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 50 g L‑aspartic acid in 900 mL water, adjust pH to 7.5 with 8 M NaOH, bring to 1 L, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 18‑amino‑acid mix (25×, 1 L)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 g each of the 18 amino acids (Glu‑Na, Asp, Lys‑HCl, Arg‑HCl, His‑HCl·H₂O, Ala, Pro, Gly, Thr, Ser, Gln, Asn‑H₂O, Val, Leu, Ile, Phe, Trp, Met) in 800 mL water, warm as needed, bring to 1 L, filter‑sterilize, aliquot 45 mL into 50 mL tubes, store at –20 °C; thaw working aliquots and keep at 4 °C for up to several months.

steps.title: Prepare defined NIM and AIM (50 mL each)
steps.instruction: Combine for each 50 mL: 2.5 mL Aspartate (5 % w/v, pH 7.5), 1 mL 50× 5052, 2 mL 25× M salts, 2 mL MgSO₄ (1 M), 6.25 mL 40 % glucose (NIM only), 10 µL trace metal stock, sterile water to final volume (36.64 mL for NIM, 41.89 mL for AIM); add antibiotics as in ZY media, prepare immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Add concentrated components to sterile water; do not pre‑mix stocks.
Adjust antibiotic concentrations per strain as described for ZY media.

steps.title: Day 1 – Transform chemically competent cells
steps.instruction: Thaw competent BL21(DE3) or B95(DE3) ΔAΔfabR on ice, pre‑chill two 1.7 mL tubes (5 min), set water bath to 42 °C, add 1–2 µL each of pAJE‑30‑nitroTyr (Mj or Ma) and target expression plasmid to each tube, add 50 µL cells, mix gently, incubate on ice 30 min, heat‑shock 45 s at 42 °C, return to ice 2 min, add 500 µL SOC, shake 250 rpm, 37 °C for 2 h, prepare LB/agar plates with appropriate antibiotics, plate cells (centrifuge 3 000 × g 3 min, remove 400 µL supernatant, resuspend pellet in 100 µL, plate 100 µL), dry plates 20 min near flame, incubate inverted overnight 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Thaw cells on ice.
Pre‑chill tubes.
Water bath 42 °C.
Add plasmids (1–2 µL each).
Add 50 µL cells, mix.
Ice 30 min.
Heat‑shock 45 s.
Ice 2 min.
Add 500 µL SOC.
Shake 250 rpm, 37 °C, 2 h.
Prepare LB/agar plates with strain‑specific antibiotics.
Centrifuge transformation mix, remove supernatant, resuspend, plate 100 µL.
Dry plates 20 min, incubate 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Day 2 – Inoculate starter cultures
steps.instruction: Pick several dozen colonies from each plate, add to 5 mL non‑inducing media (NIM) in 14 mL sterile tubes (BL21 → ZY NIM; B95 → defined NIM), grow 12–18 h at 37 °C, 250 rpm (do not exceed 18 h).

substeps.instruction: Prepare 50 mL NIM with correct antibiotics (see recipes).
Label 14 mL tubes, add 5 mL NIM each.
Scrape colonies with sterile tip, shake cells into media, avoid ejecting tip.
Incubate overnight 37 °C, 250 rpm, 12–18 h.

steps.title: Day 3 – Expression
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of starter cultures (target 1.5–4), prepare nitroTyr stock, make 50 mL auto‑induction media (AIM) appropriate for strain (ZY AIM for BL21, defined AIM for B95), add nitroTyr to TAG‑nitroTyr cultures to 0.5 mM, inoculate expression flasks 1:100 (0.5 mL starter into 50 mL AIM), add ~10 µL PPG2000 antifoam per 50 mL, shake 250 rpm, 37 °C for 24 h (if POI requires lower temperature, monitor OD₆₀₀ to 1.5 then shift: BL21 4–5 h, B95 5–6 h).

substeps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ (1.5–4).
Prepare nitroTyr stock (100 mM).
Prepare 50 mL AIM (ZY or defined) as in recipes.
Add nitroTyr to cultures needing incorporation (final 0.5 mM).
Inoculate 1:100 (0.5 mL starter → 50 mL AIM).
Add one drop (~10 µL) PPG2000 antifoam.
Incubate 37 °C, 250 rpm, 24 h.
If lower temperature needed, watch OD₆₀₀; after reaching ~1.5 shift temperature (BL21 after 4–5 h, B95 after 5–6 h).

steps.title: Day 4 – Harvest and analyze
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ and sfGFP fluorescence (excitation 485 nm, emission 510 nm); centrifuge cultures 5 000 × g 20 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellets in lysis buffer (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 5 mM imidazole, 10 % v/v glycerol), freeze pellets or proceed to purification; typical yields: ~10 mg sfGFP WT, 1–5 mg sfGFP TAG per 50 mL.

substeps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ and fluorescence of sfGFP WT and TAG150.
Centrifuge 5 000 × g, 20 min, 4 °C.
Remove supernatant, resuspend pellet in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 5 mM imidazole, 10 % glycerol.
Freeze at –80 °C or proceed to purification.

steps.title: Validate nitro‑tyrosine incorporation
steps.instruction: Purify His₆‑tagged proteins using TALON resin per manufacturer, assess color (yellow/green indicates nitroTyr), run SDS‑PAGE for purity, perform intact mass spectrometry after desalting into 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate with PD‑10 column; compare observed mass to expected (e.g., sfGFP nitroTyr150 ≈27 921.4 Da).

substeps.instruction: Purify with TALON resin following standard protocol.
Observe color of purified protein (yellow/green = successful nitroTyr).
Run SDS‑PAGE to confirm full‑length protein.
Desalt samples into 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate using PD‑10 column.
Submit for intact MS; verify mass matches nitroTyr‑containing protein.

description: Validation of protocol Evaluation of nitroTyr encoding efficiency For this protocol, the sfGFP proteins were purified following standard (i.e., manufacturer recommendation) TALON resin protocols. Once purified, sfGFP WT should be green, and sfGFP nitroTyr150 should be yellow/green ( Figure 3 ). A yellow color for your purified POI would indicate successful encoding of nitroTyr, but by itself does not confirm homogenous encoding. A lack of color in the purified POI with nitroTyr could indicate the nitroTyr on your protein was reduced to aminoTyr, near-cognate suppression occurred instead of nitroTyr (when using B95(DE3) cells), or the nitroTyr was encoded at a position where the phenolic oxygen is protonated, which quenches its color [24,25]. See Troubleshooting for more information. Figure 3. sfGFP WT and sfGFP nitroTyr150 after standard TALON purification Following protein purification, protein purity and encoding fidelity should be assessed. Protein purity is easily evaluated by SDS-PAGE gel analysis. The fidelity of nitroTyr encoding is evaluated by intact (i.e., whole-protein) mass spectrometry. In this protocol, intact mass spectrometry is used as the primary method because it enables assessment of the relative abundance of correctly encoded nitroTyr-containing protein compared with aminoTyr or mis-encoded species. For intact mass spectrometry, protein samples should be desalted into a mass spectrometry–compatible buffer to remove nonvolatile components. Here, sfGFP proteins were desalted into 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate using a PD-10 column according to the manufacturer’s protocols. Optimal sample preparation conditions may vary depending on instrumentation and should be determined in consultation with your mass spectrometry facility.
